notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); this package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), and no hardware was attached or run.

WHAT IT SERVES: the ReachUR5-v0 task of gh.edvardsz/ur5_gym as a simulated R0 world.sim driver. The repository registers ReachUR5-v0 with the out-of-clone entry point gym_ignition.runtimes.gazebo_runtime:GazeboRuntime (src/gym_ur5/__init__.py:8-18); the card's in-clone entry symbols are the task classes, and the first, gym_ur5.tasks.reach:Reach (src/gym_ur5/tasks/reach.py:22), is this driver's native. The driver serves cap.world.reset.v1 {seed, options} -> {observation, seed}, cap.world.seed.v1 {seed} -> {seed, accepted}, and cap.world.step.v1 {ticks, action: {values: [3]}} -> {observation, reward, terminated, truncated, tick, state_hash}. The action is bounded to Box(-1, 1, shape=(3,)) (reach.py:39-42); ticks keeps the class schema's 1..10000 bound; the 100-step episode limit (src/gym_ur5/__init__.py:11) is replicated in step().

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card is family-config with the GymnasiumDriver helper, but this package is a direct Driver over the task class. The actual Gym environment class is the external GazeboRuntime, not in the clone, and the task classes do not define reset/step/close; a GymnasiumDriver fake would implement env methods absent from the task class, which G7 can only report as MAYBE_ABSENT warnings because the task's base task.Task is external. A direct Driver over gym_ur5.tasks.reach:Reach keeps the fake to the task's own methods and passes G7 with no warning.

WHY A FAKE: the card's mock_strategy prefers the upstream simulator, but the package may never import or run the clone, and the gate has no Ignition Gazebo, gym-ignition or network. backends['fake'] is .fake:FakeReach, a kinematic stand-in that applies the task's own action arithmetic (reach.py:50-74) to a point end effector and reimplements get_observation, get_reward, get_info, is_done, reset_task and the position getters with the task's constants; it does not run Gazebo, IK, joint controllers or Fuel downloads, and it was not compared with an upstream run. The upstream sim backend was not run.

NOT COVERED: the Gazebo rigid-body dynamics, contacts, joint controllers, inverse kinematics and model assets; the RedPoint target randomization (the fake's start and target are fixed placeholder test data, so a seed is recorded and echoed but does not change the fake's scene); the other two registered environments ReachDictUR5-v0 and PickAndPlaceUR5-v0 (their dict observations, finger actions and cube respawn); rendering, cameras/images and Fuel downloads; snapshot/restore (the task class has no get_state/set_state; fidelity.snapshot_restore is false). Nothing was validated against a real UR5 or RG2.

WARNINGS: the only gate warning is G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1; the task class has no seed method, so the seed only sets the next reset's seed (the runtime reads the state for every receipt). It is the expected simulator-seed warning (PLAYBOOK.md section 8). No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised. G1-G5 and G7-G9 passed.

TESTS: test_driver.py keeps mhs.testing.check_driver and adds ten cases (first-step auto-reset, 0.1 scaling and workspace clamp, the 0.05 reward boundary, seed echo and repeat, the 100-tick truncation and PRECONDITION refusal, the action envelope and a schema-invalid action, the e-stop latch, the state fields and the published fidelity contract); they pass.

STATE: simulated R0, set from the three catalogue classes (cap.world.reset/seed/step are R0) and the card's R0 floor; no hardware arm is driven. No x-cap id was used, so there are no catalogue_requests, and there is no site-limits.example.json because no bound is operator-required.
